north_star: A portable, auditable research-orchestration and evidence workbench that can operate standalone and can ingest from or hand off to Department systems without requiring Virginia Tech infrastructure.
deployment_assumptions: Virginia Tech ARC is a development/classroom convenience, not an end-product dependency.
Department users may already have enterprise media analytics, generative-AI, data catalog, and approved collection capabilities.
No undocumented Northstar, StateChat, OpenNet, or other Department API is assumed to exist.
Integration must therefore be adapter-based and support file interchange even when direct APIs are unavailable.
The product must remain useful when one or more external collectors or LLM services are unavailable.

public_basis.supports: Northstar exists as a Department digital/news/social-media analytics capability.
StateChat is an enterprise generative-AI capability and the Department has multiple existing AI/media-analysis workflows.
INR seeks requirements-driven OSINT, use of Department/IC data catalogs, collaboration, citation tracking, responsible governance, and reduced redundancy.
The Enterprise Data Catalog is a central OpenNet repository for discovery and access to shareable Department data assets.
Department enterprise data management emphasizes discoverable, accessible, interoperable, securely shared data.

requirements.title: No Virginia Tech runtime dependency
requirements.requirement: The delivered State profile must not require Virginia Tech ARC, Virginia Tech credentials, ARC OnDemand, or any Virginia Tech-only service for normal operation.
acceptance: A clean Windows or macOS installation can launch and perform non-LLM workflows without Virginia Tech credentials.
LLM-backed workflows can use a non-VT provider or a documented custom provider interface.
ARC-specific guidance is presented as a classroom/development option rather than the product default for State delivery.

requirements.title: Complement existing Department systems
requirements.requirement: SUGAR must be able to complement existing Department collection, analytics, and AI systems rather than require SUGAR to replace them.
acceptance: Collection, model inference, evidence management, and reporting remain separable layers.
An external dataset can enter the evidence pipeline without being recollected by a SUGAR platform collector.
A SUGAR evidence package can be exported without requiring the recipient to run the SUGAR desktop application.
requirements.verification: architecture review and external-data integration test

requirements.title: Canonical inbound data interface
requirements.requirement: SUGAR must provide a documented inbound adapter for externally collected public-source records with explicit schema validation and provenance preservation.
acceptance: Import at minimum JSONL and CSV into a documented canonical record shape.
Reject or quarantine records missing required source identity/provenance fields instead of silently inventing them.
Preserve supplied native IDs, URLs, timestamps, source names, query/collection context, and original text where available.
Record importer name/version and import time in provenance metadata.

requirements.title: Portable outbound evidence package
requirements.requirement: A completed research run must export an application-independent evidence package suitable for handoff, review, or downstream ingestion.
acceptance: Package includes a machine-readable manifest, normalized evidence, analytic outputs, provenance, limitations, and human-review state.
Core tabular data is exportable in CSV and/or JSONL without proprietary serialization.
Package documents schema versions and software version.
A reviewer can inspect the package without access to Virginia Tech infrastructure.

requirements.title: Provider-neutral AI boundary
requirements.requirement: LLM-assisted features must depend on a provider interface rather than Virginia Tech ARC or a single commercial model.
acceptance: OpenAI, a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and no-LLM operation are supported deployment paths.
Provider/model identity is recorded with AI-generated artifacts.
Failure of the configured model service does not corrupt evidence or convert missing AI output into a factual finding.
No StateChat API or other internal Department API is assumed until an interface is actually provided.

requirements.title: Research-question-first workflow
requirements.requirement: The primary State workflow must begin from a research requirement rather than requiring the user to design a keyword matrix manually.
acceptance: User can specify question, geography, timeframe, target audience, languages, known entities, and collection constraints.
SUGAR can generate an inspectable initial search plan from that requirement.
The original requirement is stored with the project and all downstream runs.

requirements.title: Auditable adaptive search planning
requirements.requirement: Search expansion, retirement, and pivot decisions must be inspectable and tied to evidence rather than hidden inside an unconstrained agent loop.
acceptance: Each generated query records parent concept/query, rationale, origin, and status.
Branch continuation or retirement records measurable reasons such as relevance yield, novelty, duplication, source diversity, or coverage gain.
Discovered concepts cannot drift arbitrarily away from the original research requirement without explicit evidence and bounded-hop rules.
The analyst can pause, edit, exclude, or approve search branches.
requirements.verification: deterministic planner fixtures and audit-log review

requirements.title: End-to-end provenance
requirements.requirement: Every State-facing finding must be traceable from analytic claim to source evidence and the collection/import context that produced it.
acceptance: A finding can enumerate supporting and contradicting evidence IDs.
Evidence retains source URL/native identity, publication/collection time where available, and collection/import provenance.
Generated summaries never replace the stored original evidence.
Exports preserve the claim-to-evidence linkage.
requirements.verification: evidence-lineage tests and manual package audit

requirements.title: Coverage and limitation reporting
requirements.requirement: SUGAR must distinguish observed absence from collection failure and explicitly report important coverage gaps.
acceptance: Reports distinguish unavailable, failed, partial, and successful collection surfaces.
Coverage can be summarized by source, language, geography, timeframe, and research concept when those dimensions are available.
No access failure is represented as zero activity.
State-facing briefs include material collection limitations by default.
requirements.verification: collector failure fixtures and report tests

requirements.title: Human review and AI labeling
requirements.requirement: Observed facts, calculations, AI classifications/inferences, and human analytic judgments must remain distinguishable throughout the workflow.
acceptance: AI cannot self-verify evidence or silently promote a hypothesis into a verified finding.
High-consequence claims require explicit supporting evidence and human review state.
AI provider/model and relevant prompt/workflow version are recorded for reproducibility.
State-facing output clearly labels uncertainty and review state.

requirements.title: Public/authorized access and data minimization
requirements.requirement: SUGAR must operate within public or explicitly authorized access boundaries and minimize unnecessary personal data collection.
acceptance: Collectors fail closed at unsupported authentication, anti-bot, or access-control boundaries.
Secrets are not written into portable project manifests or ordinary logs.
The default State workflow is ecosystem/audience oriented and does not create person dossiers unrelated to the research requirement.
Imported datasets retain handling/usage metadata when supplied.

requirements.title: Portable reproducible projects
requirements.requirement: A project must remain inspectable, moveable, and rerunnable across machines without hidden local state being required for its evidentiary record.
acceptance: Research requirement, query/search plan, evidence, assessments, limitations, and outputs are registered in the workspace.
Portable paths are relative to the project root unless explicitly marked external.
Missing artifacts remain visible as missing rather than being silently removed.
A project records software/schema versions needed to interpret its outputs.

requirements.title: Non-developer installation
requirements.requirement: Ordinary State-profile users should not need Python, Git, an IDE, or manual package installation to launch the desktop product.
acceptance: Windows and macOS packaged builds include their required runtime components.
First-run diagnostics identify missing optional credentials/services without crashing.
Core project inspection and import/export remain available without configuring an LLM.

requirements.title: Documented extension interfaces
requirements.requirement: A maintainer should be able to add a collector, external-data importer, model provider, or exporter without modifying unrelated platform-specific UI logic.
acceptance: Collector interface is documented and registry based.
Inbound importer interface is documented once implemented.
Model-provider boundary is documented.
At least one small example extension exists for each public extension point.

requirements.title: Saved monitoring and change detection
requirements.requirement: Users should be able to rerun a saved requirement and distinguish meaningful change from ordinary corpus churn.
acceptance: Saved requirement and collection constraints can be rerun.
Comparison reports identify new/declining actors, narratives, source coverage, and material evidence changes where supportable.
A changed collector/access state is reported separately from a substantive change in the information environment.

requirements.title: Concise evidence brief
requirements.requirement: The default State-facing output should be a short evidence brief with drill-down rather than a long opaque generated report.
acceptance: Brief contains a short BLUF, key findings, confidence/review state, what changed when applicable, and collection limitations.
Each substantive finding links or references supporting evidence IDs.
Methodology details are available without dominating the first page.
requirements.verification: golden-file report tests and human review

requirements.title: Accessible desktop and report surfaces
requirements.requirement: The delivery profile should be designed toward Section 508-compatible interaction and readable exported products.
acceptance: Core desktop workflow is keyboard operable.
Text and controls remain readable in supported appearance modes and scaling settings.
Information is not encoded only by color.
Generated reports use structured headings and machine-readable text rather than image-only output.
requirements.verification: accessibility checklist and UI regression testing

requirements.title: Scriptable non-GUI workflow
requirements.requirement: Core collection, workspace, State, and analytic workflows must remain callable through stable CLI or typed service operations for automation and integration.
acceptance: Packaged/core releases expose documented CLI entry points.
Desktop clients call shared core operations rather than owning separate analytic implementations.
Automation does not require screen-driving the desktop UI.
requirements.verification: CLI smoke tests and architecture tests

requirements.title: Maintainer handoff package
requirements.requirement: The final repository must let a technically competent maintainer understand deployment, extension points, schemas, tests, and known limitations without relying on the original student team.
acceptance: Architecture, product contract, collector interface, data schemas, release process, and security boundaries are indexed from repository documentation.
A fresh maintainer can run tests and build a supported package from documented steps.
Known unsupported/internal integrations are explicitly named instead of implied.
Release artifacts include version and license information.
